title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor mediates peripheral-central neuroimmune crosstalk in autoimmune thyroid diseases.
authors: Zhang, Haiyang; Jiang, Shufan; Zhu, Tianyi; Liu, Yuting; Li, Jipeng; Fang, Sijie; Li, Yinwei; Sun, Jing; He, Xinheng; Tong, Chuanjun; Gao, Zhengrun; Fan, Xianqun; Zhou, Huifang
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过多组学与结构建模（蛋白-蛋白对接、小分子对接、简正模式）分析TSHR介导的外周-中枢神经免疫互作，虽涉及PPI与物理模拟方法，但对象为折叠蛋白TSHR而非无序蛋白/IDR，且未聚焦相分离或无序介导的互作机制，仅部分可迁移启发。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Organ-specific autoimmune diseases, particularly Graves' disease (GD) and its extrathyroidal manifestation, Graves' orbitopathy (GO), are characterized by systemic autoimmunity that may extend its impact to the central nervous system (CNS). While thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR) is the primary driver of pathological remodeling in the thyroid and orbital tissues, emerging evidence suggests it is also expressed in the brain and may participate in neuroimmune signaling. However, the molecular mechanisms linking peripheral TSHR-driven autoimmunity to these extended systemic features remain unclear. Thus, GD and GO provide a unique window to investigate how peripheral autoantibodies influence CNS involvement as part of its broader pathological spectrum. METHODS: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and post-GWAS analyses were integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and brain imaging phenotypes to comprehensively characterize peripheral and central alterations in GD and GO. Mendelian randomization was applied to test causal relationships between genetic variants and brain signatures. Structural biology analyses were further conducted including protein-protein docking, small-molecule docking, and normal mode dynamics to identify prospective modulators of TSHR. Immunofluorescence staining was performed in a GO mouse model to validate the colocalization of potential interacted proteins in the specific brain region. RESULTS: Brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) alterations in GO and GO were systematically analyzed to identify neuroanatomical and functional alterations. TSHR was further identified as a shared genetic driver across peripheral and central compartments. TSHR was expressed in spiny projection neurons, microglia, and peripheral T cells, with cell-cell communication analyses highlighting TSHR-mediated interactions among neurons, endothelial cells, and microglia. Immunofluorescence staining in a GO mouse model confirmed the colocalization of TSHR with FN1 and GNAS in the basal ganglia, providing tissue-level validation of the computationally predicted ligand-receptor interactions. Immune profiling further showed immune alterations in GD and GO. Structural modeling supported plausible physical interfaces between TSHR and interacting proteins, and small-molecule screening identified three repurposable compounds - venetoclax, irinotecan, and dutasteride - with predicted favorable docking scores and stable binding poses in our simulations. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that TSHR acts as a molecular hub mediating peripheral-central neuroimmune crosstalk in GD and GO. The results support a broader "disease-molecule axis" framework that links genetic susceptibility with multi-level immune and neural mechanisms. This work provides mechanistic insights relevant to the development of TSHR-targeted therapies, with implications for both peripheral immune modulation and central regulation. However, the limited sample size, lack of longitudinal follow-up, and absence of in vivo validation warrant cautious interpretation and further investigation.
abstract_zh:
背景：器官特异性自身免疫疾病，尤其是格雷夫斯病（Graves' disease, GD）及其甲状腺外表现——格雷夫斯眼病（Graves' orbitopathy, GO），以可能扩展至中枢神经系统（central nervous system, CNS）的系统性自身免疫为特征。尽管促甲状腺激素受体（thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor, TSHR）是甲状腺和眼眶组织中病理重塑的主要驱动因素，但新近证据表明其也在脑中表达，并可能参与神经免疫信号传导。然而，连接外周TSHR驱动的自身免疫与这些扩展性系统性特征之间的分子机制仍不清楚。因此，GD和GO为研究外周自身抗体如何影响CNS参与其更广泛的病理谱系提供了一个独特窗口。

方法：将全基因组关联研究（genome-wide association studies, GWAS）及后GWAS分析与批量RNA测序、单细胞和空间转录组学以及脑影像表型相结合，以全面表征GD和GO中的外周和中枢改变。应用孟德尔随机化检验遗传变异与脑信号之间的因果关系。进一步开展结构生物学分析，包括蛋白质-蛋白质对接、小分子对接和简正模式动力学，以识别TSHR的潜在调节因子。在GO小鼠模型中进行了免疫荧光染色，以验证潜在相互作用蛋白在特定脑区的共定位。

结果：系统分析了GO和GD中脑影像衍生表型（imaging-derived phenotypes, IDPs）的改变，以识别神经解剖学和功能性变化。进一步将TSHR确定为外周和中枢区室共有的遗传驱动因素。TSHR在棘状投射神经元、小胶质细胞和外周T细胞中表达，细胞间通讯分析突出了TSHR介导的神经元、内皮细胞和小胶质细胞之间的相互作用。GO小鼠模型中的免疫荧光染色证实了TSHR与FN1和GNAS在基底节中的共定位，为计算预测的配体-受体相互作用提供了组织水平验证。免疫谱分析进一步显示了GD和GO中的免疫改变。结构建模支持TSHR与相互作用蛋白之间合理的物理界面，小分子筛选识别出三种可再利用化合物——维奈托克（venetoclax）、伊立替康（irinotecan）和度他雄胺（dutasteride），在我们的模拟中具有预测的有利对接评分和稳定结合姿态。

结论：这些发现表明，TSHR作为介导GD和GO中外周-中枢神经免疫串扰的分子枢纽。结果支持一个更广泛的“疾病-分子轴”框架，将遗传易感性与多水平免疫和神经机制联系起来。这项工作为TSHR靶向疗法的开发提供了机制性见解，对外周免疫调节和中枢调控均具有意义。然而，样本量有限、缺乏纵向随访以及缺少体内验证，需谨慎解读并开展进一步研究。
